pixel_observations: One roughly circular bulb with several closely spaced boundary strokes: an exterior glass wall and an inner conducting-film boundary. The circular body opens into a long narrow downward neck around the central needle.
A hollow-looking pump sidearm branches left from the lower neck. Two horizontal branch boundary runs connect to the neck; a separate leftward arrow between them denotes the vacuum-pump direction.

One slim hatched metal needle rises vertically from below the bottom of the neck to a tip near the circular body's center. Its shaft exits the visible bottom neck. The image does not resolve an insulating seal, feedthrough mechanism, hidden joint, or pump internals.

Fifteen distinguishable illustrative rays converge at the central tip and terminate at the inner circular boundary. Clockwise through the upper fan from the lower-left endpoint: lower-left oblique, left horizontal, shallow upper-left, steeper upper-left, northwest diagonal, steep northwest, near-up-left, up vertical, near-up-right, steep northeast, northeast diagonal, steeper right-up, shallow right-up, right horizontal, lower-right oblique.
Arrowheads on the fan point away from the needle tip toward the sphere. The fan spans the upper region and both lower lateral directions, not a full downward fan through the needle.
The conducting-film label is at upper right with an oblique leader terminating at the upper-right ring/inner-wall region.
The metal-needle label is lower left inside the bulb; its oblique leader runs up-right toward the tip/upper needle region.
The ion-trajectory label is right of the needle below the fan. A bent/bracket-like leader beside the right rays identifies that family; this annotation is not an extra ion path.
The vacuum-pump label is left of the neck beside the sidearm. The leftward flow arrow identifies that branch without depicting a pump body.
The glass-bulb label is at lower right with an up-left leader ending on the lower-right exterior shoulder of the bulb.

There are no printed plus/minus signs, numerical radii, pressure or voltage labels, named points, angle marks, calibration ticks, atom markers, screen-impact dots, or photographic atom images in this source PNG.

A smaller irregular/wavy tip-surface stroke near the lower middle contains tiny hill-like bumps. Lowercase a is beside the left projection-ray intersection and lowercase b beside the right nearly vertical projection-ray intersection.

The two labelled projection directions run from the common bottom vertex through a to A and through b to B. Arrowheads indicate outward travel toward the screen; the long oblique and vertical lines are not separate particle populations.
A separate leftmost sloping radius line joins the common vertex to an unlabelled point on the outer screen, with an outward endpoint arrow and the label R along it.
A separate right-up short radius line joins the same vertex to an unlabelled point on the small surface, with an outward endpoint arrow and the label r along it.

An alpha mark sits between the two labelled projection rays, above the tip surface. A short cross-ray curved/connector mark indicates their included angle. No numerical angle or radian unit is printed in the source.
The helium-ion-trajectory label is upper right; branching leader strokes point to the two labelled projection directions, rather than to a third trajectory.
The tungsten-atom label is on the right at mid-height, with a slanting leader toward the small hill-like surface/feature near the b region.
A and B have heavy visible endpoint marks; a and b are identified around the small surface intersections, where thick low-resolution strokes prevent precise boundary/center metrology.

The source does not draw a separate exact circular construction arc through a and b. Its small physical-surface stroke is visibly irregular; no complete atom outline or calibrated microscopic photograph is present.

R is the sphere radius and r the tip's radius of curvature. The shared angular factor is in radians for AB = R alpha and ab = r alpha.
